body:
maya: starting rollout v2.3.1 -> targeting 10% canary for 'narrow-path' feature-flag (new_infer_path=on for 10%). will watch metrics for 10m

deploy-bot: deploy started: release/v2.3.1 -> env=prod -> canary=10% (build: sha@c3f9a2)

sasha: getting an alert about error_rate SLO but the observability dashboard for 'inference-slo' panels are blank for this timeframe, can anyone see the dashboard? :eyes:

infra-bot: alert triggered: SLO error budget burn > 3% (5m window) for service=inference (severity=warning)

eli: I can see traffic spike to variant B in logs. but panels referencing `variant` tag return empty results — wonder if tag name changed in the release

jon: which alert exactly? I only got a flood from the synth-monitoring job which looks unrelated (lots of 5xx from synthetic checks). could be masking the real canary signals

rachel: @ops-rotations can you confirm paging? I got a pager for SLO burn but no useful dashboard to triage.

ops-rotations: paging right now. silencing synth-monitoring alerts on pagerDuty for 30m to reduce noise, will post when done. :no_bell:

maya: confirming — errors started ~2m after canary flip. logs show `model-serving: timeout` for variant B.

jon: tried to toggle the flag to off for the 10% cohort via admin console — UI says success but traffic still routes to new path. suspect propagation issue between FF service and routing layer.

eli: quick test: curling edge to check headers

```bash
curl -s -D - https://api.redwood/internal/route-check -H "x-ff-new_infer_path: true" | head
```

response shows `x-routing: variant-b` for 10% of requests

maya: can someone apply emergency kill-switch? we need to force all traffic to stable variant until we confirm root cause.

jon: doing kill-switch now via admin API

```bash
curl -X POST "https://feature-flags.redwood/api/v1/flags/new_infer_path/force" -d '{"state":"off","ttl":3600}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```

jon: API returned 200. propagation logs show broadcast to routers but still seeing a small tail of variant-b. rolling logs show edge cache TTLs.

maya: deploy-bot: consider rollback? if flag kill doesn't converge fast enough.

deploy-bot: rollback triggered: releasing previous stable: release/v2.3.0 -> rollback start

maya: rollback started, but error rate only dropped ~30% so far — still seeing elevated 5xx. possibly warmed-up KV caches or stuck connections.

sasha: important note: the 'inference-slo' dashboard queries `metric_name:request.latency{deploy_tag:*}`. this release removed `deploy_tag` dimension briefly during build -> panels returned no data and people assumed alerts were false positives. we lost immediate visibility.

eli: yep I grep'd the ingestion logs — `deploy_tag` metric dimension was missing for ~6m because of a metric rename in the exporter. monitoring team already has that exporter change in this build.

rachel: OK, customer impact numbers: from tracing we see ~115 failing requests/min during peak window (~07:12-07:20 UTC). that's ~0.6% of total request volume. estimate affected customers ~18 (most hit edge retries). no revenue-critical customers reported errors yet.

pm-alejandra: please confirm SLA impact. do we have any 5xx spikes hitting paid customers? need to notify CS if so.

sasha: no paid-customer 5xx escalations in last 30m on slack or support. I'll message CS with the numbers and ask them to preemptively notify any heavy users.

ops-rotations: synth-monitoring silence in effect. un-silencing once we have dashboards back to avoid missing followups. also added an ephemeral route to mute frontend-alerts for this incident.

jon: follow-up: the reason kill-switch lagged was routers honoring a `stale_route_ttl=90s` for existing connections; so tail traffic persisted. will note in runbook.

infra-bot: synthetic check: latency 95p -> returned to normal at 07:25 UTC; error-rate normalized to baseline by 07:28 UTC

maya: who wants to own the incident doc/postmortem? we need root-cause (metric rename + feature-flag propagation + route TTL) and action items.

els: I'll own the postmortem, will include proposed guards: pre-deploy monitoring smoke tests for dashboard panels, and a feature-flag force propagation check with verification hooks.

jon: action item: add a fast-path kill endpoint for routers that bypasses stale_route_ttl when an emergency flag is set. PR drafted: https://git.internal/redwood/routers/pulls/442

sasha: action item: add dashboard alert that fires if primary SLO panels return empty (query returns no data) — 'dashboard-sanity-check' alert.

rachel: action item: CS notify and short post to customers who may have seen degraded responses. I'll draft the message with @pm-alejandra.

ops-rotations: handing off to next on-call (weekend shift) — summary: mitigated by feature-flag kill + rollback, dashboards briefly blinded due to metric rename, noisy synth alerts silenced, customer impact low. see notes in #incident-tracker.

ops-rotations: @maya @eli i'm passing on the channel; will ping in 30m if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-15T07:10Z created -> status: mitigated -> severity: sev2 -> owner: eli -> link: https://incidents.redwood/1954443210

maya: thanks team. please add the retro items to the postmortem and tag ops + monitoring for follow-up. closing hands-on phase now.
